title: Fully polynomial-size LP relaxation scheme for maximum knapsack
formal: Does every maximum zero-one knapsack instance admit, for every rational \(0<\varepsilon<1\), an objective-independent rational extended LP relaxation of total bit size polynomial jointly in the input length L and \(1/\varepsilon\), whose gap is at most \(1+\varepsilon\) for all nonnegative profit vectors?
definitions:
The input is nonnegative integral weights a_1,…,a_n and capacity b, all in binary. Let \(F=\{x\in\{0,1\}^n:a^{\mathsf T}x\le b\}\); the empty selection makes it nonempty. L counts the encodings of weights, capacity, dimension and the rational accuracy parameter. A relaxation is a rational linear system in (x,z), with arbitrary auxiliary continuous variables, whose projection R satisfies \(\operatorname{conv}(F)\subseteq R\subseteq[0,1]^n\). The same R must be used for every real profit vector c≥0, and satisfy \[\max_{x\in R}c^{\mathsf T}x\le(1+\varepsilon)\max_{x\in F}c^{\mathsf T}x.\]This also requires a zero LP optimum whenever the integral optimum is zero.

Size is the entire binary rational description, including equations, inequalities, variables and coefficients. There must be universal C,k such that size≤C(L+1/epsilon+1)^k for all instances and accuracies. The exponent cannot depend on epsilon. This bit-size choice is an explicit strengthening of inequality-count-only size. Only existence is asked, with no efficient-construction requirement; the input may contain overweight or zero-weight items.
answer_criterion: Give a complete Lean-checked proof of a jointly polynomial-size scheme and its simultaneous gap guarantee, or refute it. Bounds with an exponent depending on 1/epsilon and lower bounds confined to formulations without auxiliary variables do not settle this target.
context:
Bienstock’s approximation scheme motivates the distinction between polynomial size at each fixed accuracy and polynomial dependence on reciprocal accuracy.

Faenza and Sanità show limitations in the original variable space; extended formulations are explicitly allowed here.
why: A fully polynomial formulation scheme would provide one compact geometric certificate for all objectives.

import_provenance.original_statement: Can maximum 0–1 knapsack be approximated simultaneously for every nonnegative profit vector by an objective-independent extended LP of size polynomial in n and 1/ε with gap at most 1+ε? Bienstock’s polynomial-size schemes for each fixed ε leave this stronger analogue of an FPTAS unresolved.
